panels.title: Segment Frontiers
panels.description: Which segment each position is in. A position is a (segment, entry) pair, split across this panel and Entry Frontiers because a Prometheus gauge holds one number - read the two together. write = highest acknowledged; compacted / truncated = how far cleanup has got; read = one series per reader.

panels.title: Entry Frontiers
panels.description: How far into its segment each position is - the entry half of the (segment, entry) pair whose segment half is in Segment Frontiers. Entry ids restart at 0 in every new segment, so these curves saw-tooth: a drop to zero is a segment roll, not a reset. For the same reason, lag is measured in segments rather than entries.

How many segments each reader is behind the write frontier. Entry ids restart at every segment, so an entry-level difference across a segment boundary is meaningless; segment lag is not. The write frontier is aggregated with max because every process that opens a log publishes one, readers included: without it the match group holds one series per process and the query fails.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, woodpecker_id, log_ns, log_id) (woodpecker_client_write_frontier_segment{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}) - on(namespace, woodpecker_id, log_ns, log_id) group_right() woodpecker_client_read_frontier_segment{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}

panels.title: Reader Segment Lag

targets.expr: (sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_append_latency_count{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[5m])) - sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_append_latency_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", le=~"256(\\.0+)?"}[5m]))) / sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_append_latency_count{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[5m]))

(sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_append_latency_count{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[5m] offset 7d)) - sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_append_latency_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", le=~"256(\\.0+)?"}[5m] offset 7d))) / sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_append_latency_count{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[5m] offset 7d))

panels.title: C1/C2 · Share of appends slower than 256 ms
panels.description: C1 is the solid reading against the 1% line: more than one append in a hundred slower than 256 ms. C2 is the same quantity a week earlier, drawn alongside so the comparison the rule makes -- now above three times then -- is something you can see rather than compute. The line only applies to C1; C2 has no fixed level, which is the point of it: a region that normally sits at 0.01% is in trouble at 0.5% long before it reaches 1%.

panels.title: C3 · Pending append ops
panels.description: The queue caps at 10000, so half full is the warning.

targets.expr:
sum by (log_ns, log_id) (
  changes(woodpecker_client_write_frontier_segment{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[5m])
+ clamp_min(delta(woodpecker_client_write_frontier_entry{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[5m]), 0)
)

panels.title: C4 · Write frontier movement, 5m
panels.description: Movement of the write frontier, counted as segments rolled plus entries advanced inside the current one. Entry ids restart at zero on every segment roll (client_metrics.go:401), so a plain delta on the entry gauge goes large-negative for a healthy writer and reads 0 for one genuinely stuck -- the criterion inverted. clamp_min absorbs the reset and the segment term keeps the roll itself counted as progress. An occasional isolated spike here is expected and can be ignored: the segment and entry gauges are registered separately, so a scrape landing between the two Set calls during a roll records the new segment beside the old segment's entry id. The error only ever overstates progress, never the reverse, so it cannot hide a stall.

targets.expr: (sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_read_latency_count{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[5m])) - sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_read_latency_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", le=~"512(\\.0+)?"}[5m]))) / sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_read_latency_count{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[5m]))

panels.title: C5 · Share of reads slower than 512 ms
panels.description: 512 ms is the top finite bucket of this histogram, which is why the rule counts the tail rather than asking for a p99 the buckets cannot express. The le matcher is a regex because Prometheus renders these bucket bounds as "512.0", not "512"; an exact match on the bare integer silently returns nothing.

targets.expr:
sum by (log_ns, log_id, reader_name) (
  changes(woodpecker_client_read_frontier_segment{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[10m])
+ clamp_min(delta(woodpecker_client_read_frontier_entry{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[10m]), 0)
)

panels.title: C6 · Read frontier movement, 10m
panels.description: Movement of the read frontier, counted as segments rolled plus entries advanced inside the current one. Entry ids restart at zero on every segment roll (client_metrics.go:401), so a plain delta on the entry gauge goes large-negative for a healthy writer and reads 0 for one genuinely stuck -- the criterion inverted. clamp_min absorbs the reset and the segment term keeps the roll itself counted as progress. The append rate is drawn alongside for the same reason C4 carries it: a flat read frontier is only a stall if something is being written. On an idle log both lines sit at zero and nothing is wrong. An occasional isolated spike here is expected and can be ignored: the segment and entry gauges are registered separately, so a scrape landing between the two Set calls during a roll records the new segment beside the old segment's entry id. The error only ever overstates progress, never the reverse, so it cannot hide a stall.

targets.expr: sum by (log_ns, log_id) (rate(woodpecker_client_direct_read_requests_total{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", status="error"}[5m]))

panels.title: C7 · Direct read failures
panels.description: A failed direct read falls back to a quorum read, so this degrades latency rather than correctness.

targets.expr: sum by (log_ns, log_id, reason) (increase(woodpecker_client_segment_compaction_failures_total{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}[15m]))

panels.title: C8 · Segment compaction failures, 15m
panels.description: Uncompacted means the data is still only on local disk. The reason label is a stable enum and belongs in the alert annotation.

targets.expr: min(count by (log_ns, log_id, segment_id) (woodpecker_client_active_segment_node{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"}))

min(count by (log_ns, log_id, segment_id) (count by (log_ns, log_id, segment_id, az) (woodpecker_client_active_segment_node{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns"})))

panels.title: C9 · Replicas holding each active segment
panels.description: Below the replica factor, one more failure loses the segment. The AZ series catches a quorum that is nominally three replicas but not actually spread. Colour runs the other way here because fewer replicas is worse: at or above the line the segment still has its full quorum, below it one more failure loses the segment.
